text: Public dusre parties ko sirf promises dekh ke vote kar deti hai, opposition ko mehnat karne ki zarurat nahi lagti, isliye woh aaram se power mein aa sakte hain.
documents: Why there are no protests against vote theft Fear of BJP s coercion, belief in its invincibility from rigged polls, and Hindutva s appeal make voters tolerate vote theft without protest. Opposition must offer structural economic change, not doles, to give people a lasting stake in democracy. Published May 11, 2026 16 03 IST - 8 MINS READ Supporters celebrate with party flags as they return from the swearing-in ceremony of BJP leader and West Bengal s newly elected Chief Minister, Suvendu Adhikari, in Kolkata on May 9, 2026. Photo Credit Dibyangshu SARKAR AFP On May 4, when it became palpable that the BJP was coming to power inWest Bengal, a Kolkata-based journalist-friend sought an online meeting with four other members of the team that runs a Bengali news website, which attracts a minimum of 30,000 visitors every month. Three of the five reside outside Bengal. During the meeting, the journalist-friend suggested they should start winding down their operations. The journalist-friend explained to me that having watched the BJP neuter mainstream media elsewhere, it was clear that it was only a matter of time before independent journalists were targeted in Bengal. When the accused in the Bhima Koregaon case couldn t get bail for years and Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam still can t, despite being represented by India s best lawyers, I would be forgotten if I were jailed or raided, he said. Two months ago, I was in Patna, where I met a Yadav and a Muslim who vote in a village in Ara district. Both said that over cycles of elections their booth would register at least 700 votes for the Rashtriya Janata Dal. In the 2025 Bihar Assembly election, these votes flipped. It couldn t have happened without manipulation, said one. I asked him Why didn t they protest? We would have been beaten or thrown in jail, they said. The three accounts echo what s now a truism it isn t just the opposition that s facing death, but the very idea of opposition is also withering away as the fear of the BJP mounts. Even irrefutable evidence of electoral manipulation doesn t provoke protests. Unless the opposition enables the people to overcome their fear of the BJP, its winters out of power will only grow longer. The fear of the BJP has been built through a three-step process. One, the BJP has a penchant for deploying instruments of coercion to suppress dissent. Two, at least the 2024 Lok Sabha election onwards, the party is widely perceived to have acquired state power through electoral manipulation. This has given the BJP an air of invincibility. Three, and more importantly, Hindutva, or the narrative of building aHindu rashtra, has become the wish of a large segment of the Indian electorate. They are immune to the horror of watching Indian democracy die. Consider these details in the 2024 Lok Sabha and Assembly elections, held simultaneously in Odisha, the difference between the votes polled and votes counted ranged from 1 to 908 in 58 Assembly booths (according to Biju Janata Dal s press note). And this, when the BJD could lay hands on a very limited number of Form 17Cs, which provides the count of votes cast in every booth. The voter turnout was revised upward over two days, ranging from around 7 per cent to over 17 per cent in the State s 21 Lok Sabha constituencies, and from 8.54 per cent to 30.64 per cent in its 147 Assembly seats. Public intellectual Parakala Prabhakar persuasively showed that in Andhra Pradesh, approximately 17.19 lakh people voted between 11.45 pm and 2 am in 3,500 booths for both the Lok Sabha and Assembly elections, which were held simultaneously in 2024. Parakala calculated that every person cast two votes in six seconds, an impossibility. The gains of the BJP-led National Democratic Alliance in Odisha and Andhra Pradesh swept it to power. Without public anger being expressed over perceived electoral manipulation, the BJP turned the Election Commission of India (ECI) into a customised eraser, for deliberately effacing voters unlikely to vote for it. It was brazen in West Bengal, about which much has been written. It s a mug s game to determine the degree to which the Special intensive Revision (SIR) contributed to Mamata Banerjee s ouster from power. In a healthy democracy, such evidence of electoral rigging would have led to an outburst of rage. It hasn t happened in India. One reason is that the parties constituting the opposition are led or populated by second-generation dynasts untrained in the politics of agitations and movements. Lacking the stamina and fortitude to struggle and suffer, their default response has been to petition a body they themselves accuse of electoral manipulation the ECI. Or appeal to the Supreme Court, which rarely rules against a strong executive, once again reflected in its decision to facilitate the SIR. But even if they were to overcome their own limitations, they are unlikely to succeed unless they neutralise Hindutva, the alternative to the idea of a secular, plural, multicultural India. It is now India s largest political constituency, whose members do not consider the establishment of a Hindu rashtra, even through means fair or foul, to be repugnant. The opposition has tried four methods to wean away supporters of Hindutva. Its leaders play the devout Hindu by publicly displaying their reverence for Hinduism. Their religious personae, in contrast to that they sported in the past, seem hypocritical and convince few. Some ceased to speak of the othering of Muslims, hoping to counter allegations of favouring them. But their silence doesn t impress the Hindutva constituency. A few have pitted caste and regional-linguistic identities against Hindutva, but the BJP portrays them as forces dividing Hindus and even India. Almost all opposition leaders harp on the danger of Hindutva fomenting social instability. These strategies gloss over one fundamental truth Hindutva and its politics of religious polarisation demonise religious minorities, activists subscribing to progressive ideologies, and dominant caste groups opposed to the BJP Yadavs in Uttar Pradesh and Bihar, and Jats in Haryana, for instance. Yet, even among them, it s the religious minorities whose lives and livelihoods are imperilled. Repression with a class-community character For most Hindus, the state s sharp edge under Hindutva isn t a threat, as it was under the Emergency, with repression having a far more widespread class-community character. It was consequently easy to build opposition against Indira Gandhi. Hindutva targets selectively, limiting the widening of social alliance opposed to it. There are also advantages in supporting the BJP. Privileged Hindu groups gain from its perspective of development and the poor receive direct benefit transfers. Dependent on Hindutva, they are invested in its survival. This bond between Hindus and Hindutva is based on residual Hindu-Muslim animosity inherited from history. The animosity has been heightened through false narratives that portray Muslims as a drag on India s rise, and as prone to violence, with militancy in Kashmir cited as an example. They are accused of disrespecting Hindu religious sentiments as they refuse to hand over temples that were allegedly turned into mosques in medieval India. A political-cultural milieu conducive to Hindu assertion has been spawned. Herein lie two lessons for the opposition to draw Hindu anxieties, real or imagined, can neither be glossed over nor pandered to. The former doesn t deter the BJP from raising contentious Hindu-Muslim issues the latter only has them to plumb for the more authentic articulator of their anxieties. On top of it, their dependency on Hindutva has them to acquiesce to its inherent authoritarianism, fearing state reprisals and loss of material benefits. The opposition s challenge is to shift away from the politics of doles to bringing about structural changes to the Indian economy. Doles enable the poor to survive but don t remove their precarity, as agriculture and land reforms, security of tenure in jobs, the end of contractual labour, etc., do. It s in this context that the manufactured crisis of Hindu identity can be more effectively addressed, for the anxieties it generates is deepened because of the hand-to-mouth existence of the underclasses. To illustrate my point, here s the example of Assam s Raijor Dal leader Akhil Gogoi, who defied the overwhelming majoritarian consolidation in Assam to win from the Hindu-numerous constituency of Sibsagar this Assembly election. Gogoi isn t a Hindu chauvinist. He has, in fact, protested against the eviction of Muslims, depicted as illegal immigrants. He argues that Hindutva would steamroll Assam s unique cultural identity, as it would gradually impose the north Indian Hindu culture on the State. Yet, his rhetoric hasn t alienated Hindus, who are nearly 75 percent in his constituency. The explanation for it lies in his agenda he asks his audience to buy clothes from shopkeepers, not shop online, for then the profits go to giant retailers he speaks of improving irrigation to introduce three cycles of crops a year, and establishing finishing schools in villages, where formal school education would be combined with skilling, and village-based industries. Citing statistics to show that large tracts of land from which Muslims were uprooted in Assam were transferred to big businesses, Gogoi frames Hindutva s politics of polarisation as a subterfuge to nourish the neoliberal economy. Just as one swallow doesn t make a summer, one MLA cannot remake a democracy. Gogoi s politics may lack the economist s finesse and his party is centred around him, yet it indicates a method of neutralising Hindutva by giving people a stake in democracy more enduring than doles do. Only then would they resist the hollowing out of democracy. Ajaz Ashraf is a senior journalist from Delhi and the author ofBhima Koregaon Challenging Caste. क्या घोषणा पत्र में कोई भी वादा कर सकते हैं राजनीतिक दल जानें क्या है चुनाव आयोग की गाइडलाइन? नई दिल्ली लोकसभा चुनाव की तारीख जारी होते ही पार्टियां घोषणा पत्र यानी मेनिफेस्टो को तैयार करने में जुट गई हैं. फिलहाल सबसे ज्यादा चर्चा कांग्रेस के घोषणा पत्र की हो रही है. कांग्रेस वर्किंग कमेटी की बैठक के बाद इस बात की चर्चा है कि पार्टी अपने चुनावी पिटारे से सच्चर कमेटी, ओल्ड पेंशन स्कीम और जांच एजेंसियों पर कानून बनाने की घोषणाएं कर सकती है. बैठक के बाद कांग्रेस नेता सचिन पायलट ने कहा कि हम अपने घोषणा पत्र में देश के हालात के बारे में भी बताएंगे. घोषणा पत्र को महज एक डॉक्यमेंट नहीं माना जाता, यह चुनावी रण को जीतने में अहम रोल निभाता है. घोषणाएं मतदाताओं को प्रभावित करती हैं और अक्सर चुनावों में यह टर्निंग पॉइंट साबित होती हैं. इसी बहाने आइए जानते हैं, क्या होता है घोषणा पत्र, कैसे बनाया जाता है, इसे बनाने के लिए चुनाव आयोग की किन शर्तों का पालन करना अनिवार्य है और सुप्रीम ने क्यों पार्टियों के मेनिफेस्टो पर क्या सवाल उठाए थे? कैसे घोषणा पत्र बनाती हैं पार्टियां?आसान भाषा में समझें तो घोषणा पत्र ऐसा दस्तावेज होता है जो चुनाव लड़ने वाली पार्टियां जारी करती हैं. इसके जरिए राजनीतिक दल बताते हैं कि सत्ता में आने पर वो क्या-क्या करेंगे. कैसे सरकार चलाएंगे. जनता को कितना फायदा होगा. इस तरह घोषणा पत्र वादों के पिटारों से कम नहीं होता, जिसे बताकर पार्टियां वोट मांगती हैं. हालांकि यह बात अलग है वो कितने पूरे होते हैं. राजनीतिक दल इसे तैयार करने के लिए एक लम्बी-चौड़ी टीम गठित करते हैं. टीम पार्टी की नीति, मुद्दे, देश की जरूरत और दूसरी पार्टियों की कमजोरी समझने का काम करती है. इन सब पर नजर रखते हुए वो ऐसी घोषणाओं का पिटारा तैयार करती है, जो मतदाताओं को रिझाए और विरोधी पार्टियों पर भारी पड़े. इसमें कौन-कौन से मुद्दे शामिल होंगे, इसको लेकर पार्टियों में कई दौर की बैठकें चलती हैं. पदाधिकारियों की रजामंदी के बाद इसे जारी किया जाता है. यह भी पढ़ें दतिया में मतदान के 5 दिन बाकी, चुनावी माहौल नदारद सुप्रीम कोर्ट के दखल के बाद बदलनी पड़ी गाइडलाइनभारत से अलग दुनिया के दूसरे देशों में पार्टियां चुनावी पिटारे में आर्थिक नीति, हेल्थ को बेहतर बनाने की घोषणा और शासन में सुधार करने के साथ कई मुद्दों का जिक्र करती हैं, जिससे सीधे-सीधे मतदाताओं को कोई लालच नहीं दिया जाता है. लेकिन भारत में कई बार घोषणा पत्रों में ऐसे वादों का जिक्र किया गया जिसे पूरा करना या तो नामुमकिन सा था या फिर राजनीतिक दल मुफ्त रेवड़िया बांटने की बात कहते थे. इसका मामला कोर्ट में पहुंचा. सुप्रीम कोर्ट में जुलाई 2013 एस सुब्रमण्यम बालाजी वर्सेज तमिलनाडु सरकार और अन्य मामले की सुनवाई हुई. जस्टिस रंजन गोगोई और जस्टिस पी सतशिवम की खंडपीठ ने सुनवाई में कहा था पार्टियों के मुफ्त विवरण यानी फ्रीबिज लोगों पर असर छोड़ते हैं. देश में अब तक कोई ऐसा प्रावधान नहीं बना जो पार्टियों को ऐसा लालच देने से रोके या ऐसी घोषणाओं को नियंत्रित कर सके.कोर्ट ने कहा था कि राजनीतिक दलों से बात करके चुनाव आयोग इस पर गाइडलाइन तैयार करे. 2013 में आयोग ने इस पर गाइडलाइन भी जारी की थी. क्या है चुनाव आयोग की गाइडलाइन?चुनाव आयोग की गाइडलाइन कहती है, घोषणा पत्र में कुछ भी ऐसा नहीं होगा जो संविधान के सिद्धांतों का उल्लंघन करे. राजनीतिक पार्टियों को ऐसे वादों से बचना होगा जो चुनाव की प्रक्रिया पर बुरा असर डालें. राजनीतिक दल अपने घोषणा पत्र में जो भी वादे बताएंगे वो कैसे पूरे होंगे इसे भी बताना पड़ेगा. वादों को पूरा करने के लिए फंड कहां से लाएंगे, यह भी बताना होगा. दुनिया के ज्यादातर लोकतांत्रिक देशों में मेनिफेस्टो को लेकर कोई सख्त कानून नहीं है. लेकिन इलेक्टोरल अथॉरिटी के पास यह पावर होती है कि वो पार्टी के मेनिफेस्टो में घोषणाओं को हटा सकती हैं. भूटान और मैक्सिको में ऐसा होता है. वहीं, UK में अथॉरिटी ने गाइडलाइन में यह बताया है कि पार्टियां चुनावी अभियान में कितनी चीजों का इस्तेमाल करेंगी-किन चीजों का नहीं. इसमें घोषणा पत्र भी शामिल है. वहीं अमेरिका में ऐसा कोई नियम नहीं है. 70 साल में Pro-BJP wave, not anti-Congress, powered 2023 Assembly election results Modi s popularity, welfare schemes, and women s votes played key roles in the BJP victory. Here s a deep-dive into the numbers and trends. Published Dec 13, 2023 13 05 IST - 11 MINS READ BJP supporters in Jabalpur celebrating the party s victory in Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, and Chhattisgarh on December 3. Photo Credit PTI The elections held in five States produced a mixed verdict, with the BJP winning in Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, and Chhattisgarh, and the Congress defeating the Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) in Telangana. The Zoram People s Movement (ZPM) defeated the Mizo National Front (MNF) in Mizoram. Although there were some possibilities of the Congress losing the elections in Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan, the party s defeat in Chhattisgarh came as a big surprise. The results send out a few important messages. First and foremost is that the Modi magic is still working. Prime Minister Narendra Modi s campaign played an important role in the BJP s victory in the three States it won. The results also reinforce the Congress inability to take on the BJP in the Hindi heartland States in a direct contest. However, the party still has a presence in the southern States. The results also indicate that the Congress failed to make the caste census an issue that resonates with common voters. The results indicate theincreasing importance of women votersin Indian elections. The Prime Minister s repeated references to that in his address to party workers after the BJP s victory is testimony to that. The verdict also points to the increasing importance of welfare schemes in the party s strategy of voter mobilisation. But the defeat of the BRS in Telangana serves as a warning that schemes alone cannot win an election but can only be icing on the cake the party needs to do other things to win the trust of the voters. Also Read Modi s heartland sweep a warning sign for complacent Congress A careful analysis of the results indicates that there was no anti-Congress wave, rather it was a pro-BJP wave. That much is clear from the vote share of the Congress and the BJP in the three States in which the Congress lost to the BJP. Congress leader Rahul Gandhi and Chief Minister Bhupesh Baghel with farm workers at a paddy field in Chhattisgarh ahead of the elections. Photo Credit PTI The Congress polled at least 40 per cent of the votes in all these States, pointing to a marginal increase in support rather than a decline compared with the 2018 Assembly elections. Despite this increase, the Congress lost to the BJP because the BJP managed to increase its vote share at the cost of regional parties and independents, displaying an increased support for the BJP in 2023 compared with the previous Assembly election. In Chhattisgarh, although the Congress retained its overall support, the BJP picked up votes in the north and south of the State for a decisive lead over the Congress. The regional analysis of the verdict in Madhya Pradesh suggests that the Congress managed to perform well in three regions, Chambal, Mahakoushal, and Malwa Nimar, which account for a total of 100 seats. But the Congress trailed behind the BJP by 14 per cent votes in the Malwa North and Madhya Bharat regions, which account for 74 seats. Similarly, it trailed behind the BJP by 10 per cent votes in Bundelkhand and Vindhya Pradesh the two regions account for 56 Assembly seats. In Rajasthan, which witnessed a close contest, the Congress trailed behind the BJP by 4-5 per cent of the votes in the south Rajasthan and Haroti regions, and it also trailed behind the BJP by a narrower margin in the western and central regions, where the regional parties and independents polled 19 per cent and 13 per cent respectively. These two regions combined account for 79 Assembly seats. In Telangana, the Congress took a decisive lead over the BRS by 6 per cent in the north and by 7 per cent in the south the two regions account for 94 seats in the 119-member House. In the Hyderabad region, which accounts for 25 seats, the BJP and the Congress won one seat each and the All India Majli-e-Ittehadul Muslimeen won seven. The division of votes between various contenders helped the BRS win 16 seats in this region. After the BJP s defeat in Himachal Pradesh in the 2022 Assembly election and in Karnataka earlier this year, the opposition tried to build a narrative that the Modi magic was declining and that his ability to pull votes for the BJP had declined significantly. But the BJP s resounding victory in the latest round of Assembly elections without projecting anyone as a chief ministerial candidate in any State, with Modi as the party s face, clearly indicates that the voters choice of the BJP as the ruling party was largely influenced by the Modi factor. Data from the Lokniti-CSDS post-election survey indicate that nearly 19 per cent of BJP voters in Madhya Pradesh voted in the name of Modi, while in Rajasthan it was 24 per cent. High levels of satisfaction with the Central government also tilted the votes in favour of the BJP. In Madhya Pradesh, 67 per cent of the voters were satisfied with the Central government in Rajasthan the figure was 79 per cent, and in Chhattisgarh 80 per cent. Many other leaders of the BJP, including its State leaders, campaigned aggressively, but the BJP s campaign was so centred on Modi that the BJP even came up with the slogan Madhya Pradesh ke man me Modi hai, Modi ke man me Madhya Pradesh hai (Modi in Madhya Pradesh s mind, Madhya Pradesh in Modi s mind). Also Read How BJP s aggressive campaign exploited Congress weaknesses to secure decisive victory in Rajasthan Congress inability to mobilise OBC votes The victory of the Congress in the 2018 Assembly elections in Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, and Chhattisgarh had raised the party s hopes of putting up a challenge to the BJP in 2019, but the Lok Sabha election results in 2019 shattered those expectations. The Congress has kept losing election after election since then. But its recent victories in Himachal Pradesh and Karnataka raised the hopes of a Congress revival even in the Hindi heartland as it was the ruling party in Rajasthan and Chhattisgarh and had accused the BJP of stealing its government in Madhya Pradesh. Another factor indicating a shift from the Congress was people s unhappiness and concern about rising prices and increasing unemployment. The Lokniti-CSDS post-election survey in all the States that went to the polls in the last couple of years clearly indicates that between 70 and 80 per cent of the voters in different States were worried about increasing prices and about 70 per cent were concerned about increasing unemployment. In Chhattisgarh, 76 per cent believed that prices had increased in Madhya Pradesh the figure was 80 per cent, while in Rajasthan it was 72 per cent. Outgoing Chief Minister Ashok Gehlot with other leaders in Jaipur on November 23. People appeared to have more faith in the promises made by Prime Minister Modi in Chhattisgarh and Rajasthan than in the benefits they actually got through schemes. Photo Credit PTI As many as 40 per cent in Rajasthan, 44 per cent in Madhya Pradesh, and 40 per cent in Chhattisgarh believed that unemployment had increased. Despite this, the BJP returned to power in most States except a few (Himachal and Karnataka being the latest). But one cannot deny the fact that unemployment and prices have been rising the Congress, it was thought, would be able to make this an issue as well as use the issue of caste census in these elections. One expected voters to show their concern on these issues while casting their vote. That did not happen. The defeat in the three Hindi heartland States means the Congress has been wiped out of north India. The Lokniti-CSDS post-election survey indicates that while the Congress may have lost the election in these States, it has managed to make inroads into Dalit and Adivasi areas except in Chhattisgarh, where the Adivasi votes tilted in favour of the BJP. In all three States, Dalits voted more in favour of the Congress than the BJP. Adivasi voters in Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh also voted for the Congress in big numbers. What hurt the Congress was its inability to mobilise OBC voters despite Rahul Gandhi championing the cause for an OBC census. The findings suggest that the OBCs did not vote for the Congress in any of the three States. The BJP s lead over the Congress among OBC voters was 9 per cent in Chhattisgarh, 12 per cent in Madhya Pradesh, and 5 per cent in Rajasthan. With Chief Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan facing 18 years of anti-incumbency, there were conflicting predictions about the electoral outcome in Madhya Pradesh. Different meanings were attached to the BJP fielding 10 MPs, including Ministers, from various Assembly constituencies in Madhya Pradesh one was that it was done to beat the anti-incumbency sentiment. The Lokniti-CSDS survey in late October showed that there was no anti-incumbency as 63 per cent of the voters liked the work done by the Shivraj Singh Chouhan government, and his popularity rating was 39 per cent against Kamal Nath s 32 per cent. The survey also indicated that Chouhan remained popular despite being sidelined during the early days of campaigning. While various factors are attributed to Chouhan s popularity, the Ladli Behna scheme is largely responsible for his massive popularity among women voters. Women voters have contributed to the BJP s victory in all three States. Women s turnout was 74 per cent in Rajasthan, 76 per cent in Madhya Pradesh, 78 per cent in Chhattisgarh, and 72 per cent in Telangana. Women not only came out in large numbers, they also voted for the BJP in slightly larger numbers than men. In Chhattisgarh, the BJP got 5 per cent more votes from women voters than the Congress, while in Madhya Pradesh the figure was 4 per cent. In Rajasthan, the BJP led by 4 per cent over the Congress among women voters. The fourth important point that emerges from the verdict is that welfare schemes play a more important role now than in the past, but schemes alone cannot win elections. Schemes plus other factors such as popularity, leadership, governance, and an overall positive perception are needed to win elections. The BJP s big win in Madhya Pradesh is largely credited to the Ladli Behna Scheme, but the Congress too had equally popular schemes in Rajasthan and Chhattisgarh, as did the BRS in Telangana, but they were defeated. The KCR government s Rythu Bandhu scheme, the Ashok Gehlot government s Chiranjeevi Health Insurance Scheme, Bhupesh Baghel s Urban Guarantee and Half Electricity Bill schemes were popular in their States but not enough to win elections. On K. Chandrasekhar Rao s birthday, in Hyderabad in February 2022. Voters in Telangana had more faith in what the Congress promised than in the benefits they were receiving from the BRS government s schemes. Photo Credit NAGARA GOPAL Survey findings indicate that among the beneficiaries of Baghel s Half Electricity Bill scheme, 44 per cent voted for the Congress, while 43 per cent voted for the BJP. Among the beneficiaries of the Ladli Behna Scheme, 51 per cent voted for the BJP, while 39 per cent voted for the Congress. In Rajasthan, among the beneficiaries of the Chiranjeevi Health Insurance scheme, 43 per cent voted for the Congress and 39 per cent for the BJP. Among the beneficiaries of the Rythu Bandhu scheme in Telangana, 43 per cent voted for the BRS while 45 per cent voted for the Congress. People appeared to have more faith in the promises made by Prime Minister Modi in Chhattisgarh and Rajasthan than in the benefits they actually got through the schemes. Similarly, voters in Telangana had more faith in what the Congress promised than in the benefits they were receiving from the BRS government s schemes. Voters in Rajasthan and Chhattisgarh seemed to show more faith in the BJP s promise than in the Congress government s delivery, which is why Modi now often refers to Modi ki guarantee matlab guarantee ki guarantee . While these defeats will certainly have a demoralising impact on the parties in the INDIA bloc, especially the Congress, they can still put up a challenge against the BJP in 2024 if they work out a seat-sharing arrangement. This seems an uphill task given the differences between the parties in the alliance. The Congress debacle does not give any positive vibes to voters about it being able to lead the INDIA alliance. Even if it manages to work out a seat-sharing arrangement, it may not be enough to challenge the BJP in 2024 the alliance needs to think of and go to the people with a positive agenda. Merely an aggressive negative campaign against the BJP and against Modi can only create an illusion of opposition. This has severe limitations and is not enough to beat the formidable BJP. भारत में चुनाव और संविधान पर प्रमुख फैसले मतदान और चुनाव लड़ने का अधिकार भारत के सुप्रीम कोर्ट ने संविधान की व्याख्या करके चुनावी प्रक्रिया और लोकतांत्रिक मूल्यों को मजबूत करने में अहम भूमिका निभाई है। राजबाला मामले में चर्चा किए गए महत्वपूर्ण फैसले चुनावी अधिकारों और विधायी शक्तियों पर मूल्यवान दृष्टिकोण प्रस्तुत करते हैं। इस लेख में उन प्रमुख फैसलों पर चर्चा की गई है, जिन्होंने चुनावों और संवैधानिक कानून को प्रभावित किया है। 1. मतदान और चुनाव लड़ने का अधिकार (Right to Vote and Contest Elections) अनुच्छेद 326 के तहत मतदान का अधिकार एक संवैधानिक अधिकार है, लेकिन मौलिक अधिकार (Fundamental Right) नहीं है। PUCL बनाम भारत संघ मामले में यह स्पष्ट किया गया कि मतदान का अधिकार संवैधानिक है, लेकिन मतदान की स्वतंत्रता अनुच्छेद 19(1)(a) के तहत अभिव्यक्ति की स्वतंत्रता (Freedom of Expression) से जुड़ी है। एन.पी. पोनुस्वामी बनाम रिटर्निंग ऑफिसर और ज्योति बसु बनाम देवी घोषाल ने यह भी बताया कि चुनाव लड़ना एक सांविधिक अधिकार (Statutory Right) है, जिसे संसद कानूनी प्रावधानों के माध्यम से नियंत्रित कर सकती है। 2. उम्मीदवारों के लिए शैक्षिक योग्यता (Educational Qualifications for Candidates) राजबाला मामले में हरियाणा पंचायत राज (संशोधन) अधिनियम, 2015 के तहत पंचायत चुनाव लड़ने के लिए शैक्षिक योग्यता (Educational Qualification) का प्रावधान एक महत्वपूर्ण चर्चा का विषय था। सुप्रीम कोर्ट ने इसे विधायी शक्ति (Legislative Power) का वैध प्रयोग माना और कहा कि विधायिका उम्मीदवारों के लिए पात्रता (Eligibility) के मापदंड निर्धारित कर सकती है। इस फैसले ने यह संतुलन बनाए रखा कि योग्य नेतृत्व (Leadership) सुनिश्चित करने के साथ-साथ चुनावी भागीदारी को भी समावेशी रखा जाए। 3. योग्यता और अयोग्यता (Qualifications and Disqualifications) अनुच्छेद 84 और 102 (और उनके राज्य समकक्ष अनुच्छेद 173 और 191) विधायिका की सदस्यता के लिए योग्यता (Qualifications) और अयोग्यता (Disqualifications) की रूपरेखा प्रस्तुत करते हैं। राजबाला मामले में अदालत ने पुष्टि की कि ये अनुच्छेद संसद को आगे के नियम लागू करने का अधिकार देते हैं, और चुनाव लड़ने का अधिकार एक सांविधिक (Statutory) अधिकार है। जावेद बनाम हरियाणा राज्य मामले में अदालत ने यह स्वीकार किया कि दो से अधिक बच्चों वाले उम्मीदवारों को अयोग्य घोषित करना नीतिगत उद्देश्यों (Policy Goals) के लिए वैध है, जैसे जनसंख्या नियंत्रण। 4. स्थानीय चुनावों का संवैधानिक दर्जा (Constitutional Status of Local Elections) 73वें और 74वें संविधान संशोधन ने पंचायत राज संस्थाओं और नगरपालिका निकायों (Municipal Bodies) को संवैधानिक दर्जा दिया। संविधान के भाग IX और IX-A में राज्य विधानसभाओं (State Legislatures) को चुनावों के लिए योग्यता और अयोग्यता निर्धारित करने की शक्ति दी गई। के. कृष्णमूर्ति बनाम भारत संघमामले में सुप्रीम कोर्ट ने माना कि स्थानीय निकाय (Local Bodies) विकेंद्रीकृत प्रशासन के लिए महत्वपूर्ण हैं, जिससे उनके चुनावी प्रक्रियाओं पर विधायी अधिकार सही ठहरता है। 5. समानता और उचित प्रतिबंध (Equality and Reasonable Restrictions) अनुच्छेद 14 कानून के समक्ष समानता की गारंटी देता है। हालांकि, चुनावी अधिकारों पर प्रतिबंध जैसे कि शैक्षिक योग्यता या आपराधिक मामलों के आधार पर अयोग्यता को उचित वर्गीकरण (Reasonable Classification) की कसौटी पर खरा उतरना होता है। श्यामदेव प्रसाद सिंह बनाम नवल किशोर यादवमामले में अदालत ने जोर दिया कि चुनाव से जुड़े अधिकार सांविधिक प्रावधानों से उत्पन्न होते हैं और उन्हें संवैधानिक सुरक्षा के तहत चुनौती देना सीमित है। 6. न्यायिक समीक्षा और विधायी विवेक (Judicial Review and Legislative Wisdom) राजबाला मामले में इस बात पर जोर दिया गया कि न्यायालय का कार्य केवल यह सुनिश्चित करना है कि कोई विधायी अधिनियम (Legislative Act) संवैधानिक है या नहीं, न कि उसके विवेक का मूल्यांकन करना। विधायिकाओं के पास ऐसे कानून बनाने का अधिकार है जो वे जनहित में मानते हैं, बशर्ते वे संविधान के प्रावधानों का उल्लंघन न करें। 7. PUCL मामला और सूचना का अधिकार (PUCL Case and Right to Information) PUCL बनाम भारत संघ मामलेमें सुप्रीम कोर्ट ने अनुच्छेद 19(1)(a) की व्याख्या का विस्तार करते हुए उम्मीदवारों की पृष्ठभूमि के बारे में जानकारी प्राप्त करने के अधिकार को शामिल किया। इस महत्वपूर्ण फैसले ने यह सुनिश्चित किया कि मतदाता सूचित निर्णय ले सकें, और यह चुनावी अधिकारों (Electoral Rights) और अभिव्यक्ति की स्वतंत्रता के बीच संबंध को मजबूत करता है। 8. आरक्षण और सामाजिक न्याय (Reservation and Social Justice) अनुच्छेद 243D और 243T स्थानीय निकायों में अनुसूचित जाति (Scheduled Castes), अनुसूचित जनजाति (Scheduled Tribes) और महिलाओं के लिए सीटों के आरक्षण का समर्थन करते हैं। यह दृष्टिकोण सामाजिक न्याय (Social Justice) और सहभागी शासन (Participatory Governance) के संवैधानिक आदेश के अनुरूप है, जैसा कि इंद्रा साहनी बनाम भारत संघ और अन्य मामलों में नीतियों के दायरे के विश्लेषण में देखा गया। इन फैसलों के माध्यम से उभरती न्यायशास्त्र चुनावी अधिकारों, विधायी शक्तियों और संवैधानिक आदेशों के बीच जटिल संबंधों को दर्शाती है। सुप्रीम कोर्ट की व्याख्याएं लगातार विकसित होती रही हैं, यह सुनिश्चित करती हैं कि चुनावी प्रक्रियाएं लोकतांत्रिक मूल्यों और संवैधानिक सिद्धांतों को बनाए रखें, जबकि व्यावहारिक और नीति-आधारित आवश्यकताओं को निर्धारित करने के लिए विधायी ढांचे की अनुमति भी दी जाए। 2025 All Rights Reserved LiveLaw

Opposition protests against SIR, calls it vote theft by government Delhi Police halted the protest a few metres from the Parliament s gates. Police detained the Opposition leaders some of whom tried to break barricades during an hour-long protest and took them to the Parliament Street Police Station. They were released later. Updated- August 12, 2025 01 35 am IST - New Delhi Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi and other Opposition leaders sit in a bus after ther were detained during the INDIA bloc s protest march to the Election Commission in New Delhi on August 11, 2025. Photo AICC via ANI Opposition parties marched to the Election Commission of India s (ECI) headquarters in New Delhi on Monday (August 11, 2025), demanding a rollback of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in Bihar, which they said was an exercise in vote-chori (vote theft) by the government and will lead to disenfranchisement. Delhi Police halted the protest a few metres from the Parliament s gates. Police detained the Opposition leaders some of whom tried to break barricades during an hour-long protest and took them to the Parliament Street Police Station. They were released later. Also read Opposition march to Election Commission of India LIVE updates This fight is not political, but it is aimed at saving the Constitution. This fight is for one man, one vote and we want a clean, pure voter list, Rahul Gandhi, Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha, said. They cannot talk as the truth is before the entire nation, he said. Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge, who was also picked up by the police, said, I don t understand what the government fears? This is a peaceful demonstration of elected members of Parliament the ECI could have met all of us together in a hall. Also read Parliament Monsoon Session Day 16 updates on August 11, 2025 The Opposition said that it had sought an appointment from the poll body. Congress general secretary (communication), Jairam Ramesh, wrote to the commission about the protest. The MPs wish to collectively meet with the Commission on a host of issues, including but not limited to Special Intensive Revision of Electoral Rolls being undertaken in Bihar and proposed to be undertaken in other states as well, his letter said. Opposition MPs protest outside Parliament after being denied permission to march to the ECI office in New Delhi on August 11, 2025. Photo Credit Sushil Kumar Verma In response, the ECI, citing space constraints, asked the Opposition to send the names of 30 persons to come for an interaction. Reacting to the limitation imposed by the poll panel, Congress leader K.C. Venugopal said, We don t even have the freedom to go to the ECI s office. They should have at least allowed us to go to the ECI s office to register our protest. The march began at 11.30 a.m. from the Parliament after both houses were adjourned early. The Opposition members gathered in the courtyard to sing the national anthem and carried placards in multiple languages. Aam Aadmi Party, which has distanced itself from the INDIA bloc, was present at the forefront of the procession. To ensure that they did not feel excluded, no INDIA bloc banners were used. Just a few metres from the Parliament gate, the Delhi Police had put up barricades. The Parliamentarians sat in protest on the road and many leaders including Samajwadi Party chief Akhliesh Yadav, Trinamool MPs Mahua Moitra, Mitali Bag, Sagarika Ghose and Sushmita Dev, and Congress MPs Sanjana Jatav and S. Jothimani scaled the barricades. They are using the police to stop us, Mr. Yadav shouted. The elderly leaders, including Mr. Kharge, Sharad Pawar of the NCP (SP) and DMK s T.R. Baalu, brought up the rear. Later in the evening, Mr. Kharge hosted a dinner for the Opposition MPs. Mr. Ramesh said the Opposition wanted to collectively present the memorandum, instead of sending a delegation. The language was clear, collectively, all Opposition MPs would like to hand over a memorandum to the ECI. Now we are not allowed to even reach Nirvachan Sadan. Right in front of Parliament, democracy is being assaulted, democracy murdered. This is too clever, cheeky reply by the ECI, he said. He added, Chunav Aayog is Chunav Aayog, it cannot be churao aayog . (Poll panel cannot steal votes.) Trinamool s Rajya Sabha Parliamentary leader Derek O Brien said that despite the appointment, Opposition MPs were not allowed to meet the panel. We were NOT ALLOWED by Modi Amit Shah s police to reach the office of the ECI. We were told we were being taken to the ECI. But instead, we were hustled into a police station. We were released at 2.10 p.m. So, the entire Opposition could not reach Parliament on time, he wrote on X. Mr. O Brien said that the Opposition had four key demands an FIR against former Chief Election Commissioner Rajeev Kumar for alleged manipulation of the voters list , digitisation of voters list, stopping the SIR, and not making political parties to share BLA-2 details (profile, contact, and photo) with the ECI, as these, Mr. O Brien alleged, reach the BJP. Samajwadi Party Supremo Akhilesh Yadav climbing over a barricade during the march to the ECI office on August 11, 2025. Photo Credit Sushil Kumar Verma Trinamool MP Ritabrata Banerjee said the government did not allow a discussion in Parliament on SIR, and even the poll panel refused to meet the Opposition. The police are deployed to stop elected representatives. This is a super emergency, he said. Rashtriya Janta Dal MP Misa Bharati questioned why there was such a heavy police presence at the protest site. She asked, You can see how the MPs misbehaved with... Under whose pressure is the Election Commission working? Why are they afraid to meet the MPs? Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Priyanka Chaturvedi, also at the protest venue, said that the ECI was running away from answering important questions. Every time we ask a question of the ECI, a BJP spokesperson responds. ECI needs to tell us, are they working at the behest of BJP or for the people of this country, she asked. ''అధికారంలో ఉన్న ప్పుడు చేసిన నిర్వాకాలే!'' . ఈ సూత్ర మే తెలంగాణ ప్ర ధాన ప్ర తిప క్షం బీఆర్ ఎస్ కు కూడా వ ర్తిస్తుంది. ఎందుకంటే.. ఎంతైనా తెలంగా ణ ప్ర జ లు కూడా చైత న్య వంతులే క దా!!. 10 సంవ త్స రాలు అధికారంలో ఉన్న బీఆర్ ఎస్ కు రైతుల క ష్టాలు క నిపించాయా? అంటే.. కేసీఆర్ ముఖ్య మంత్రిగా బాధ్య త లు చేప ట్టిన ఏడాదిలో స చివాల యానికి కూత వేటు దూరంలో ఆంజ నేయ స్వామి ఆల యం వ ద్ద ఓ రైతు ఆత్మ హ త్య చేసుకున్నారు. దీనిని నాడు సీఎం కేసీఆర్ ఎలా ట్రీట్ చేశారో తెలిసిందే. పోనీ.. ఇంటింటికీ నీటిని ఇచ్చారా? అంటే.. ప్ర శ్నార్థ క మే. నాడు అధికారంలో ఉన్న ప్పుడు రైతులు, నీళ్లు, నియామ కాలు.. వంటివి చిన్న స మ స్య లుగా మారాయి. కేంద్రంలో చ క్రం తిప్ప డం, జాతీయ రాజ కీయాలు చేయ డం.. వంటివి పెద్ద వి గా మారాయి. క ట్ చేస్తే.. ఇప్పుడు.. చ రిత్ర మ రిచిన బీఆర్ ఎస్ .. ఇంటింటికీ 24 గంట లు నీటిని ఇస్తామ ని.. రైతుల ను క డుపులో పెట్టుకుంటామ ని చెబుతోంది. మంచిదే.. ఈ మార్పు కావాల్సిందే. కానీ.. ప్ర జ లు హ ర్షిస్తున్నారా? ఒక వేళ జ నాలు మ రిచిపోయినా.. వారికి గుర్తు చేస్తున్న సోష ల్ మీడియా ను ఎవ రు తుడిచేయ గ ల రు. సో.. చరిత్ర బోధ ప డ క పోతే.. ప్ర జ ల స మ స్య లు ప ట్ట క పోతే.. ఇలానే ఉంటుంది. దీని నుంచి బీఆర్ ఎస్ పాఠాలు నేర్చుకుంటేనే.. భ విత ఉంటుంద ని విశ్లేష కులు చెబుతున్నారు.

Guide Overview Category Government Services Portal Academic Bank of Credits Estimated Time 10 min Fee Free Complete Guide Students, ABC ID (Academic Bank of Credits) ke baare me sun rahe ho aur confuse ho ki ye APAAR se alag hai ya wahi? Clear karte hain ABC ID 12-digit "digital vault" jismein tumhare college university ke credits store, transfer aur redeem hote hain (NEP 2020 ke tahat). Ye higher-education (college university) students ke liye hai aur admission enrolment me increasingly mandatory ho raha hai. Banana free hai - abc.gov.in ya DigiLocker se. Poora tarika ABC vs APAAR ka farak neeche. ABC ID Kaise Banaye (DigiLocker Se) abc.gov.in kholo (ya DigiLocker Education tab Academic Bank of Credits) Aadhaar-linked mobile number se DigiLocker pe sign-in register DigiLocker KYC authenticate karo Profile bharo apni Higher Education Institution (university college) list se chuno Generate 12-digit ABC ID ban jayegi save download karo Validity credits 7 saal tak accessible ID institutions ke beech transferable ABC ID vs APAAR ID (Confusion Clear) Cheez ABC ID APAAR ID Kya Credit vault (credits store transfer) Permanent student ID (lifelong) Kiske liye Higher-ed (college university) School se college tak, school records NEP role Credit accumulation transfer "Student account number" Link ABC APAAR ID use karta hai credits track karne ke liye Base student identifier Dono linked hain par alag - ABC credits ka bank hai, APAAR permanent identity hai. FAQs Q ABC ID card kaise banaye? A abc.gov.in ya DigiLocker (Education tab) pe Aadhaar-linked mobile se login, KYC, institution chuno, 12-digit ABC ID generate . Q ABC ID banane ki fee kitni hai? A Bilkul free - abc.gov.in DigiLocker official hai. Q ABC ID aur APAAR ID ek hi cheez hai? A Nahi - ABC ID credit vault (credits store), APAAR permanent student ID . Linked hain par alag kaam. Q ABC ID kiske liye zaroori hai? A Higher-education (college university) students ke liye - admission enrolment me increasingly mandatory. Q ABC ID kitne digit ka hota hai? A 12-digit unique ID - DigiLocker se generate hota hai. Q ABC ID DigiLocker ke bina ban sakta hai? A DigiLocker-based Aadhaar KYC hi standard rasta hai - abc.gov.in bhi DigiLocker se connect karta hai. Q Credits kitne saal tak store rehte hain? A 7 saal tak accessible ID institutions ke beech transferable hai (transfer re-admission me kaam aata hai). Q ABC ID ka photo card download hota hai? A Haan - generate hone ke baad ID card DigiLocker abc.gov.in se download save kar sakte ho. Download Now Complete Guide to e-Aadhaar Download Process Aaj ke digital yug mein, Aadhaar Card har Bhartiya nagarik ke liye sabse zaroori pehchaan patra (Identity Proof) ban gaya hai. Chahe bank account khulwana ho, SIM card lena ho, ya kisi sarkari yojana ka labh uthana ho Aadhaar har jagah anivarya hai. Lekin kya aap jante hain ki aapko hamesha physical card sath rakhne ki zarurat nahi hai? Aap e-Aadhaar ka istemal kar sakte hain. What is e-Aadhaar? (e-Aadhaar Kya Hai?) Ye aapke physical Aadhaar card ki ek password-protected electronic copy hai, jise UIDAI ke competent authority dwara digitally sign kiya jata hai. Aadhaar Act ke mutabiq, e-Aadhaar physical copy ke barabar hi valid mana jata hai. Aadhaar Card Download Kaise Karein? (Online Process) Agar aapka Aadhaar card kho gaya hai ya aapke paas physical copy nahi hai, to ghabrayein nahi. Aap niche diye gaye aasaan steps ko follow karke 2 minute mein apna e-Aadhaar PDF download kar sakte hain. Official Website Upar diye gaye orange color ke Download Now button par click karein. Enter Details Yahan aapke paas 3 option honge Aadhaar Number, Enrolment ID (EID), ya Virtual ID (VID). Apna 12-digit Aadhaar number dalein. Captcha Verification Screen par dikh raha security code (Captcha) dhyan se bharein. OTP Verification Send OTP button dabayein. Aapke registered mobile number par ek 6-digit ka OTP aayega. Verify Download OTP enter karein aur Verify Download par click karein. Aapka e-Aadhaar PDF format mein download ho jayega. e-Aadhaar PDF Password Kya Hota Hai? Bahut se log Aadhaar download to kar lete hain lekin PDF khul nahi pati kyunki wo password-protected hoti hai. Iska password bahut simple hota hai. Forgot your Aadhaar Number (UID) or Enrolment ID (EID)? Use your registered mobile number to get it back via SMS in seconds. Retrieve UID EID How to Retrieve Lost Aadhaar Number (UID) or Enrolment ID (EID) Have you lost your physical Aadhaar card and cannot remember your 12-digit Aadhaar number? Or perhaps you have applied for a new Aadhaar card but lost the acknowledgement slip containing the Enrolment ID (EID)? Do not worry. The Retrieve Aadhaar number EID SID service allows you to recover these details online instantly. This feature is a lifesaver for those who have misplaced their documents and need to download their e-Aadhaar urgent. By using this facility, your lost Aadhaar number or EID is sent directly to your registered mobile number. Important Prerequisite To use this online facility, your Mobile Number or Email ID MUST be registered and linked with your Aadhaar. If your mobile number is not linked, you cannot receive the OTP required for retrieval. Difference Between UID and EID Term Full Form Description UID Unique ID This is your final 12-digit Aadhaar Number . Select this if you already had a card. EID Enrolment ID This is the 28-digit number from your acknowledgement slip (for new applications). Step-by-Step Process to Retrieve Lost Aadhaar (UID) Visit the Official Portal Click on the Retrieve UID EID button above to open the official page. Select Retrieval Option Choose Aadhaar Number to find your main ID or Enrolment ID if you are tracking a new application. Enter Personal Details Enter your Full Name exactly as it is printed on your Aadhaar card. Enter Contact Info Captcha Enter your Registered Mobile Number or Email ID, fill the Captcha, and click Send OTP . Get SMS After OTP verification, your Aadhaar Number (UID) or EID will be sent to your mobile via SMS. Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) Q Can I retrieve my Aadhaar if I don t have my mobile number? Ans No, the online facility works strictly via OTP. If your mobile is not linked, you must visit an Aadhaar Enrollment Center with your identity proof. Q Is there any fee for this service? Ans No, the Retrieve Aadhaar EID service is completely free of cost on the myAadhaar portal. Verify Mobile Email Not sure which mobile number is linked to your Aadhaar? Verify it instantly to ensure you receive OTPs for all government services. Verify Now How to Verify Mobile Number Email Linked with Aadhaar In today s digital India, your Registered Mobile Number is the key to accessing almost all Aadhaar services. Whether you want to download your e-Aadhaar, update your address online, or verify your ITR, the OTP (One Time Password) is sent to this linked number. However, people often change their SIM cards or forget which mobile number they gave at the time of enrollment years ago. The Verify Email Mobile service on the myAadhaar portal solves this confusion. It allows you to check if the mobile number or email ID you currently possess is the one linked to your Aadhaar database. ℹ Important Clarification This service does NOT show you the mobile number linked to your Aadhaar (for privacy reasons). Instead, YOU have to enter a mobile number, and the system will tell you if it matches the records or not. It is a verification tool, not a search tool. Step-by-Step Process to Verify Mobile Number Follow this simple procedure to confirm your linked contact details Access the Service Click on the green Verify Now button above. Select Verification Type You will see two options Verify Mobile Number and Verify Email Address . Select the one you want to check. Enter Details First, enter your 12-digit Aadhaar Number . Then, enter the Mobile Number (or Email) that you think is linked. Security Check Enter the Captcha code exactly as shown in the image box. Send OTP Click on the Send OTP button. Check the Result The system will display a success or error message based on your input (explained below). Understanding the Result Messages After submitting, you will see one of these two messages. Here is what they mean Scenario 1 Match Found (Success) The mobile number you have entered is already verified with our records. Meaning Congratulations! The mobile number you typed IS the one linked to your Aadhaar. You can receive OTPs on this number. Scenario 2 No Match (Failure) The mobile number you have entered does not match with our records. Meaning The number you typed is NOT linked. Either you linked a different family member s number, or an old number that you have lost. Why is this Verification Important? 1. Fraud Prevention Ensuring that no unknown mobile number or email is linked to your ID protects your biometric and demographic data. 2. Banking Services To link Aadhaar with a bank account or PAN card, the OTP validation is mandatory. Verifying ensures you are using the correct SIM. 3. Updates You cannot update your address or download Aadhaar online if you don t know which number receives the OTP. Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) Q The system says Record not found . What should I do? Ans This means the mobile number you are entering is incorrect. Try entering mobile numbers of your family members. If none match, you must visit an Aadhaar Seva Kendra to check or update your number. Q Can I update my mobile number using this service? Ans No. This service is only for verification . To update or change your mobile number, biometric authentication is required, which can only be done offline at a center. Report Death Deactivate Aadhaar Secure the identity of your deceased family member. Officially report the death to UIDAI to prevent misuse of documents. Report Now How to Report Death of a Family Member for Aadhaar Deactivation The Aadhaar card is a unique identity proof that remains valid for a lifetime. However, in the unfortunate event of a family member s demise, it is the responsibility of the legal heir or guardian to inform the Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI). The Report death of a family member service allows you to officially flag an Aadhaar number for deactivation. This is a crucial step to ensure that the deceased person s identity documents are not misused for financial fraud, illegal SIM card issuance, or identity theft. Why is Deactivating Aadhaar Important? Many people often overlook this step, but keeping a deceased person s Aadhaar active can lead to several complications Prevent Misuse Scammers often look for dormant identities to open fake bank accounts or take loans. Subsidies Benefits To prevent the continued transfer of government benefits (like pensions) to a deceased person, which can later lead to legal recovery issues. Closure of Records It helps in closing other linked official documents like PAN Card and Voter ID systematically. Important Requirement To use this service, you MUST have a valid Death Certificate issued by the Registrar of Births and Deaths. The details on the Death Certificate must match the Aadhaar details of the deceased. Procedure to Report Death Online UIDAI has simplified the process by allowing family members to initiate this request via the myAadhaar portal. Follow these steps Login to Portal The reporting family member (Applicant) must login to the myAadhaar portal using their Own Aadhaar Number and OTP. You cannot login using the deceased person s Aadhaar. Select the Service On the dashboard, locate and click on the Report death of a family member card. Enter Details of Deceased Enter the 12-digit Aadhaar Number of the deceased family member. You may also need to provide their Name and Date of Birth as per records. Upload Document Upload a clear scanned copy (PDF JPG) of the Death Certificate . Ensure the file size is within the permissible limit (usually 2MB). Review Submit Verify all the details entered. Once submitted, you will receive a Service Request Number (SRN) to track the status. What Happens Next? (Verification) Reporting the death online does not instantly deactivate the Aadhaar. The request goes through a verification process 1. Registrar Verification The details are cross-verified with the birth and death registration records. 2. Deactivation Once verified, the UIDAI will permanently deactivate the Aadhaar number of the deceased. 3. Confirmation You can check the status using the Check deceased Aadhaar deactivation status service on the same portal. Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) Q Can anyone report the death? Ans Usually, only immediate family members (spouse, children, parents) whose mobile numbers are linked or who can prove the relationship can initiate this request. Q Is it mandatory to deactivate Aadhaar after death? Ans While there is no strict penalty currently, it is highly recommended for safety and to close the financial and legal footprint of the deceased. Q Can I reactivate the Aadhaar later if reported by mistake? Ans No. Once an Aadhaar is marked as Deceased and deactivated after proper verification, it cannot be reactivated. Please use this service carefully. LIMITED TIME OFFER Free Document Update Is your Aadhaar 10 years old? Upload Proof of Identity Address documents online for FREE till 14 06 2026. Update Now Document Update Upload PoI and PoA Online Has it been more than 10 years since you got your Aadhaar card made? Have you updated your documents recently? If not, the Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI) strongly recommends that you update your Proof of Identity (PoI) and Proof of Address (PoA) documents. Keeping your documents updated ensures that your demographic information (Name, Address, DOB) in the Aadhaar database is accurate and up-to-date. This helps in seamless verification for banking, passport services, and government subsidies. Special Offer Free Service! This online document update service is FREE OF COST till 14 06 2026 . (Note If you visit an offline Aadhaar Center, you will have to pay 50.) Which Documents do you need to upload? You need to upload one document for Identity and one for Address. Common valid documents include 1. Proof of Identity (PoI) To verify your Name and Photo. PAN Card e-PAN Driving License Passport Voter ID Ration Card (with Photo) Mark Sheet School Certificate 2. Proof of Address (PoA) To verify your Current Address. Electricity Bill ( 3 months) Water Bill ( 3 months) Gas Connection Bill Bank Passbook Statement Passport (Address page) Voter ID Step-by-Step Process to Update Documents Online Take advantage of the free window and update your documents from home using these steps Login to myAadhaar Click the Update Now button above and login using your Aadhaar Number OTP. Select Document Update Click on the Document Update card. Review your current details (Name, Address, DOB). Upload Files Scan your PoI and PoA documents. Supported formats are JPEG, PNG, or PDF (Size 2MB). Submit Since the service is free, skip the payment. Click submit. You will get a Service Request Number (SRN) . Online vs Offline Update Comparison Feature Online (myAadhaar Portal) Offline (Aadhaar Center) Cost FREE (till 14 06 2026) 50 (Service Charge) Convenience From Home (24 7) Visit Wait in Queue Documents Self Scan Upload Originals Verified by Operator Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) Q My address has changed. Can I use this service? Ans No. This service is ONLY to upload documents for existing details. To change your address, use the Address Update service. Q What happens if I don t update? Ans Your Aadhaar might get suspended or face difficulties in KYC authentication for banks or ration services. Generate Virtual ID (VID) Protect your privacy! Create a temporary 16-digit Virtual ID to use instead of your Aadhaar Number for authentication. Generate VID VID Generator Create Virtual ID to Hide Aadhaar Number Are you worried about sharing your 12-digit Aadhaar number everywhere? Do you want to protect your privacy while performing e-KYC? The Virtual ID (VID) is the solution. The VID Generator service allows you to create a temporary, revocable 16-digit random number mapped to your Aadhaar number. It can be used in lieu of your Aadhaar number for authentication services. This ensures your actual Aadhaar number remains hidden from the service provider. Privacy Feature When you use a VID, the agency (like a telecom operator or bank) cannot store your Aadhaar number. They only get a UID Token , which makes your data much more secure against leaks. Difference Aadhaar Number vs Virtual ID (VID) Feature Aadhaar Number (UID) Virtual ID (VID) Length 12 Digits (Permanent) 16 Digits (Temporary) Validity Lifetime valid Valid until you generate a new one Security Directly linked to biometric data Masks the actual Aadhaar number How to Generate or Retrieve VID Online You can generate a new VID or retrieve an existing one using the myAadhaar portal. Follow these steps Login to Portal Visit the myAadhaar dashboard by clicking the Generate VID button above. Select VID Generator Click on the VID Generator icon from the services menu. Choose Option You will see two options 1. Generate New VID If you want to create a fresh 16-digit number. 2. Retrieve Existing VID If you already generated one but forgot it. Confirm Receive Select your choice. Your 16-digit Virtual ID will be sent immediately to your Registered Mobile Number via SMS. Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) Q Is VID accepted everywhere? Ans Yes, as per government regulations, all agencies (Banks, Telecom, Govt) must accept VID for authentication. Q What happens if I generate a new VID? Ans The moment you generate a new VID, your old VID gets automatically cancelled. You can only have one active VID at a time. Q Does VID expire? Ans No, a VID does not expire by itself. It remains valid until you choose to generate a new one. Lock Unlock Aadhaar Worried about identity theft? Temporarily Lock your Biometrics or Aadhaar Number instantly for maximum security. Secure Now Lock Unlock Aadhaar Secure Your Biometrics Instantly Security is a major concern for Aadhaar holders. What if someone gets hold of your Aadhaar number and tries to misuse it? To prevent unauthorized authentication, UIDAI provides a powerful feature Lock Unlock Aadhaar . This service allows you to temporarily Lock your UID (Aadhaar Number). Once locked, no one (not even you) can perform authentication using the Aadhaar number. It acts as a digital shield against identity theft. You can Unlock it whenever you need to use it. MUST READ BEFORE LOCKING Do not lock your Aadhaar without generating a Virtual ID (VID). Once your Aadhaar is locked, you CANNOT use your Aadhaar number to unlock it (because the number itself is locked). You will compulsorily need a 16-digit Virtual ID (VID) to perform the Unlock process. Difference Aadhaar Lock vs Biometric Lock Many people confuse these two services. Here is the difference Feature UID Lock (Aadhaar Lock) Biometric Lock What it blocks? Blocks ALL authentication (Demographic, Biometric, OTP). Blocks ONLY Fingerprint and Iris scan. OTP still works. How to use when locked? You must use Virtual ID (VID) . You must temporarily Unlock biometrics to use fingerprint iris. Security Level Highest (Total Lock) Medium (Protects Biometrics only) Step-by-Step Guide to LOCK Aadhaar Generate VID First As mentioned, ensure you have a valid VID. If not, use the VID Generator service first. Open Lock Service Click the Secure Now button above and select the Lock UID option. Enter Details Enter your 12-digit Aadhaar Number, Full Name, and Pin Code. Verify OTP Enter the security captcha and click Send OTP . Enter the OTP received on your mobile. Confirmation Your Aadhaar Number is now LOCKED. You will not be able to perform authentication using the UID anymore. Step-by-Step Guide to UNLOCK Aadhaar Select Unlock UID Go to the same service page and select the Unlock UID tab. Enter VID (Not Aadhaar Number) Here, you CANNOT enter your Aadhaar number. You must enter your 16-digit Virtual ID (VID) . Verify Unlock Enter the Captcha and OTP. Once verified, your Aadhaar number will be active again. Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) Q Can I download e-Aadhaar if my UID is locked? Ans Yes, but you will have to use your Virtual ID (VID) to download it, as the Aadhaar number will not be accepted by the system. Q I forgot my VID and my Aadhaar is locked. What do I do? Ans You can use the Retrieve VID service via SMS. Send an SMS RVID Last 4 digits of Aadhaar to 1947 from your registered mobile number. Bank Seeding Status Are you receiving government subsidies? Check if your Aadhaar is successfully linked and mapped with your bank account for Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT). Check Status Bank Seeding Status Check Aadhaar-Bank Linking for DBT Many government schemes in India transfer money directly to beneficiaries bank accounts using the Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) system. This money is sent using the Aadhaar Payment Bridge (APB). For this to work, simply having a bank account is not enough. Your Aadhaar number must be seeded or mapped with that specific bank account in the NPCI (National Payments Corporation of India) database. The Bank Seeding Status service helps you check which of your bank accounts is currently linked to receive government funds. Why is Bank Seeding Essential? If your Bank Seeding Status is Inactive , you will NOT receive funds for PM Kisan Samman Nidhi LPG Gas Subsidy (PAHAL) Scholarships Pension Schemes (Old Age Widow) MNREGA Wages How to Check Bank Linking Status Online You can verify your current NPCI mapping status instantly through the myAadhaar portal. Follow these steps Login to Portal Click the Check Status button above and login using your Aadhaar Number OTP. Select Bank Seeding Status Locate and click on the Bank Seeding Status icon on the dashboard. View Result The system will display the Bank Name, Seeding Status (Active Inactive), and the Date of Linking. Understanding Your Status Result Status ACTIVE Your Aadhaar is successfully mapped. You are eligible to receive DBT funds in the mentioned bank account. Status INACTIVE Your mapping has been disabled or expired. You will NOT receive subsidies until you re-link it. My Status is Inactive Not Linked. How to Link? Note You CANNOT link your bank account to Aadhaar online via the UIDAI website. This must be done through your bank. Method 1 Visit Bank Branch (Recommended) Go to your bank branch, fill out the Aadhaar Seeding Form (DBT Mandate form), and attach a copy of your e-Aadhaar. Ask the official to Enable DBT specifically. Method 2 Net Banking Mobile App Some banks (like SBI, HDFC, ICICI, PNB) offer an option in their Net Banking App under Service Request Link Aadhaar Enable DBT . Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) Q I have accounts in 3 banks. Which one will receive the money? Ans Government benefits are sent to the Last Seeded Bank Account . If you recently linked a new bank account, the money will start coming to that new account automatically. Q My bank says Aadhaar is linked (KYC done), but status shows Inactive. Why? Ans Linking for KYC and Linking for DBT are different. You must specifically ask the bank to Map Aadhaar to NPCI for DBT . Q How long does it take to update the status? Ans Once the bank processes your request, it usually takes 2-3 working days for the status to reflect on the myAadhaar portal. Track Your PVC Card Ordered your Aadhaar PVC Card? Track its printing and delivery status in real-time. Know exactly when it will reach your doorstep. Track Order Check Aadhaar PVC Card Order Status Track Delivery Have you recently ordered the new, durable Aadhaar PVC Card online by paying 50? If yes, you might be wondering when it will reach your home. The Check Aadhaar PVC card order status service allows you to track the progress of your printing request and its dispatch status. The entire process, from ordering to delivery, typically takes 5 to 15 working days . This tool helps you know exactly where your card is whether it is still printing or has been handed over to the post office. You Need Your SRN (Service Request Number) To check the status, you must have the 28-digit SRN . This number was generated when you successfully placed the order and paid the fees. It is available on the acknowledgement slip you downloaded. How to Check PVC Order Status Online Follow these simple steps to track your application Open the Tool Click on the Track Order button above. Enter SRN Enter the 28-digit Service Request Number (SRN) carefully. Security Check Type the Captcha code shown on the screen. Submit Click on Submit . The system will verify your request and display the current status. Understanding the Status Meanings Payment Successful Your order has been received by UIDAI. In Process Your data has been sent for printing. Dispatched Your card has been printed and handed over to India Post. (This is the most important status). How to Track via India Post (Speed Post) Once the status shows Dispatched , the portal will display an Airway Bill Number (AWB) . This is your tracking ID. Copy the Airway Bill Number (AWB). Visit the India Post Tracking website (indiapost.gov.in). Enter the AWB number in the Consignment Number field. You will see the exact location of your card and the expected delivery date. Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) Q I lost my SRN. How can I check the status? Ans If you lost the SRN, check your SMS history for messages from UIDAI. Or check the Payment History section if you were logged in. Q The status says Dispatched but I haven t received it yet. Ans Delivery speed depends on India Post services. Use the Airway Bill Number to track it on the India Post website for real-time updates. Check Aadhaar Status Applied for a new Aadhaar or updated details? Track your application status in real-time using your Enrolment ID (EID) or URN. Check Status Check Aadhaar Enrolment Update Status Online Have you recently applied for a new Aadhaar card? Or have you updated your Name, Address, or Date of Birth at an Aadhaar Center? If yes, you don t need to visit the center again to know if your request is processed. The Check Enrolment Update Status service allows you to track your application in real-time. Whether you did the update online (via myAadhaar portal) or offline (at a Seva Kendra), you can track it here. Which Number Do You Need for Tracking? Depending on how you applied, you will have one of the following numbers 1. Enrolment ID (EID) Found on the top of the Acknowledgement Slip given at the Aadhaar Center. It contains 14-digit Enrolment No. 14-digit Date Time. 2. Service Request Number (SRN) Generated when you initiate an Online Update (like Address or Document Update) on the myAadhaar portal. It starts with S . 3. Update Request Number (URN) Generated via SMS if you updated details using the Self Service Update Portal (SSUP) in the past. How to Enter EID Correctly (Very Important) Most users fail to check status because they enter the EID incorrectly. The 28-digit EID is a combination of the Enrolment Number and Timestamp. Format Enrolment Number Year Month Day Time Example If slip says Date 15 08 2024, Time 14 30 55, Enrolment 1234 56789 01234 Enter like this 12345678901234 20240815 143055 (Notice the Date is reversed YYYY-MM-DD). Step-by-Step Tracking Process Follow these steps to know your current status Open the Tool Click on the Check Status button above. Enter ID Type your EID (28 digits), SRN, or URN in the box provided. Ensure there are no spaces or slashes. Security Check Enter the Captcha code exactly as shown. Submit Click Submit . The status will appear on the screen. What Does Your Status Mean? In Process Your application is still being verified by the backend team. This usually takes 5-30 days. Completed Congratulations! Your update is successful. You can now Download Aadhaar to see the changes. Rejected Your request was declined. This usually happens due to wrong documents or data mismatch. You will have to apply again. Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) Q I lost my Acknowledgement Slip. How can I get my EID? Ans You can use the Retrieve EID UID service to get your Enrolment ID on your registered mobile number. Q How many days does it take to update Aadhaar? Ans As per UIDAI guidelines, up to 90 of updates are processed within 30 days. However, in some cases, it can take up to 90 days. Q Status shows Completed but I didn t get the card by post. Ans Completed means the data is updated online. The physical letter delivery takes extra time. You can download the e-Aadhaar immediately. Check Deceased Aadhaar Deactivation Status Once you have formally reported the death of a family member to UIDAI for Aadhaar deactivation, it is important to verify if the request has been processed. The Check Deceased Aadhaar Deactivation Status service allows legal heirs or guardians to track the progress of their application. Deactivating the Aadhaar of a deceased person is a critical step to prevent identity fraud and ensure that government records are updated accurately. Requirement You will need the Service Request Number (SRN) that was generated when you submitted the Report Death request. How to Track Deactivation Request Access the Tool Click on the Check Deceased Aadhaar Deactivation Status card on the myAadhaar dashboard. Enter SRN Input the 28-digit Service Request Number provided during the reporting process. Captcha Enter the security code displayed on the screen. View Status The system will show whether the request is Pending Verification , Approved (Deactivated), or Rejected (due to document mismatch). Secure 256-bit Encryption Biometric Face Auth Supported Access Document Update Status Manage Family Profiles SSO Portal Login SSO ID User ID Password Use your camera to scan your face or upload a photo for verification. (Single Sign-On Login) SSO (Single Sign-On) ek aisa digital authentication system hai jo users ko sirf ek ID aur Password ke zariye kai saari sarkari aur private websites par login karne ki suvidha deta hai. Chahe wo Aadhaar Card Download ho, Ration Card ki jankari ho, ya Jan Aadhaar portal SSO Login se sab kuch ek jagah manage hota hai. Bharat mein digital services badhne ke saath, SSO ID Login ab har nagarik ke liye zaroori ho gaya hai. Is portal par aap apne Aadhaar number ya Face Auth ka upyog karke securely login kar sakte hain. New Update Ab aap bina password yaad rakhe, seedhe apne Chehre (Face Auth) ya Biometric se SSO Login kar sakte hain. SSO ID Registration Account Kaise Banayein? Agar aapke paas abhi tak SSO ID nahi hai, to aap niche diye gaye steps follow karke apna naya account register kar sakte hain Upar diye gaye SSO Login box mein Create New Account par click karein. Apna 12-digit Aadhaar Number enter karein. Aapke registered mobile par ek OTP aayega, use verify karein. Apna manpasand SSO User ID aur Password set karein. Registration complete hone par aap turant login kar sakte hain. Benefits of SSO Portal (SSO Ke Fayde) All-in-One Access Ek hi login se 100 services ka labh uthayein. Recover Forgotten Password Agar password bhool gaye, to Aadhaar OTP se reset karein. High Security Two-factor authentication (2FA) aur Identity verification. SSO Login FAQs Q Main apna SSO ID Password bhool gaya hun, kya karun? Ans Aap Forgot Password link par click karke apne registered mobile number ya Aadhaar OTP ke zariye apna password reset kar sakte hain. Q Kya SSO Login ke liye Aadhaar zaroori hai? Ans Haan, security verification ke liye Aadhaar card number ya Jan Aadhaar ID ka hona anivarya hai. Q SSO ID se main kaunsi services use kar sakta hun? Ans Aap Aadhaar PVC order, Address Update, Scholarship forms, Job applications, aur Electricity bill payment jaisi suvidhayein use kar sakte hain.
